transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Nice to meet you too. Well, I’m here because... ever since they made me the acting workflow lead at my job, things have just been really difficult. 

I walk into the warehouse and I'm already tense before I even clock in. I find myself snapping over little SAP errors, and I'm missing cycle-count deadlines that I never, ever used to miss. And then by the time my shift is over and I go home, I'm just too drained to do anything. I haven't been playing basketball or even working on my sketches. It's just taking a lot out of me.
Have you been feeling sad or hopeless nearly every day?

No, I wouldn't say I feel sad or hopeless every day. It's more just... stress and frustration, I guess. I'm just really worn out from all the pressure at work, but I don't feel like, you know, completely hopeless about life or anything like that. Just overwhelmed by this new role.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about several different areas of your life, not just your new role at work?

No, not really. It's pretty much just the job. I mean, I'm not sitting around worrying about my bills or my health or my family or anything like that. Everything else is mostly fine. 

It's really just... being the workflow lead. That's what's keeping me on edge. Outside of that, I don't really have anything else stressing me out. I'm just too tired from work to actually enjoy the rest of my life right now.
When did these symptoms first begin relative to becoming the acting workflow lead?

Well, the lead role started right after the team merger we had. And I'd say within the first month or two of that happening, I could already tell I just wasn't handling work the way I normally do. It started pretty quickly after I took on the new position.
